title: Point2 raised $136M to solve AI’s wiring problem. Its RF cables beat copper on reach and optics on latency.
excerpt: Point2 raised $136M Series B with Arm, Nvidia, LB Investment, and Maverick Silicon. Its e-Tube RF cables offer 10x reach vs copper and 1,000x lower latency than optics.
content_html:
TL;DR

Point2 raised $136M Series B led by LB Investment with Arm, Maverick Silicon. Backers include Nvidia, Bosch, Molex. e-Tube RF cables: 10x copper reach, 3x lower optics power, 1,000x lower latency. For rack-scale AI compute interconnect.

Point2 Technology has raised $136 million in total Series B financing to commercialise a new type of cable that could replace both copper and optics inside AI data centres. The latest extension was led by LB Investment, with new strategic participation from Arm and continued support from Maverick Silicon. The investor roster now includes Nvidia, Arm, UMC Capital, Molex, and Bosch Ventures. When the companies building AI chips, chip architectures, connectors, and automotive sensors all invest in the same cable startup, the signal is that wiring has become the bottleneck.

Point2’s e-Tube platform uses RF signaling over plastic waveguides instead of copper wire or optical fibre. The numbers are stark: 10x the reach of copper at comparable cost, 5x lower weight, and 2x less cable volume. Against optics, it claims 3x lower power, 3x lower cost, and 1,000x lower latency without the reliability problems of failing lasers. Lumilens raised $700 million for optical interconnects earlier this month, betting that light is the answer. Point2 is betting that RF can do the same job cheaper, cooler, and faster at rack scale.

“As AI systems scale and bandwidth demands reach terabit-per-second speeds, interconnect has become the defining bottleneck,” CEO Sean Park said. Arm’s SVP of strategic ventures, Paul Williamson, framed the investment around the full stack: “The next generation of AI infrastructure will rely on advances across the entire technology stack, from compute to memory and interconnect.” The funding will accelerate commercialisation of Point2’s Active RF Cable, near-packaged e-Tube, and co-packaged e-Tube solutions for rack-scale compute systems.

The AI data centre buildout has consumed hundreds of billions of dollars in chips, power, and cooling. The power crunch is sending data centre builders to the banks, and every watt saved on interconnect is a watt that can go to compute. Point2’s pitch is that the industry is spending on faster chips while the cables between them have not kept up. Whether RF over plastic waveguides can scale to the volumes that hyperscalers need is the execution question. The investor list suggests the industry thinks it can.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

Point2 筹集了由 LB Investment 领投、Arm、Maverick Silicon 领投的 1.36 亿美元 B 轮融资。 支持者包括英伟达、博世、莫仕。 e-Tube RF 电缆：铜缆长度提高 10 倍，光学功率降低 3 倍，延迟降低 1,000 倍。 用于机架级 AI 计算互连。

Point2 Technology 已筹集了总计 1.36 亿美元的 B 系列融资，用于将一种新型电缆商业化，这种电缆可以取代人工智能数据中心内的铜缆和光纤。 最新的延期由 LB Investment 牵头，Arm 进行了新的战略参与，并得到了 Maverick Silicon 的持续支持。 目前，投资者名单包括 Nvidia、Arm、UMC Capital、Molex 和 Bosch Ventures。 当构建人工智能芯片、芯片架构、连接器和汽车传感器的公司都投资于同一家电缆初创公司时，信号表明布线已成为瓶颈。

Point2 的 e-Tube 平台使用塑料波导而非铜线或光纤发送射频信号。 这些数字是显而易见的：在同等成本下，铜的覆盖范围是铜的 10 倍，重量减轻 5 倍，电缆体积减少 2 倍。 与光学相比，它声称功耗降低了 3 倍，成本降低了 3 倍，延迟降低了 1,000 倍，而且不会出现激光器故障的可靠性问题。 Lumilens 本月早些时候为光学互连筹集了 7 亿美元，押注光就是答案。 Point2 认为 RF 可以在机架规模上以更便宜、更凉爽、更快的速度完成同样的工作。

首席执行官 Sean Park 表示：“随着人工智能系统的规模和带宽需求达到每秒太比特的速度，互连已成为决定性的瓶颈。” Arm 的战略风险高级副总裁 Paul Williamson 围绕整个堆栈进行了投资：“下一代人工智能基础设施将依赖于整个技术堆栈的进步，从计算到内存和互连。” 这笔资金将加速 Point2 的有源射频电缆、近封装 e-Tube 和用于机架级计算系统的联合封装 e-Tube 解决方案的商业化。

人工智能数据中心的建设在芯片、电力和冷却方面消耗了数千亿美元。 电力紧缺正在将数据中心建设者送到银行，而互连上节省的每一瓦特都可以用于计算。 Point2 的宣传是，业界正在投资更快的芯片，但它们之间的电缆却没有跟上。 塑料波导上的射频能否扩展到超大规模企业所需的容量是执行问题。 投资者名单表明业界认为可以。
